blocks.body: DirectEatz is a full-featured POS and online ordering system designed for restaurants of all sizes. From menu management to order processing, loyalty programs to real-time reporting, everything you need is in one place. No contracts, no hidden fees — you only pay for the days you use it.
What DirectEatz Includes

items: Online ordering portal for your customers
Admin dashboard to manage orders, menu, staff, and settings
Real-time order board with sound notifications
Customer loyalty programs and promotions
Receipt printing
Sales reporting and billing
Offline-capable with automatic sync when connected

blocks.body: Getting Started

If you are a new restaurant, use the Auto Onboarding flow to set up your restaurant in minutes. You will create your account, add your restaurant details, set up your menu, and be ready to take orders — all in one guided process.
Once your restaurant is set up, log into the admin dashboard (Tablero) to manage orders, update your menu, configure promotions, add staff, and customize your settings.
Understanding the Dashboard

The admin dashboard is organized into groups accessible from the left sidebar: Orders (order board) for live orders, New Order to create customer orders, Reporting for sales data, Dashboard for billing and display settings, Settings for restaurant setup, menu, printers, tables, and personnel, and Marketing for promotions, loyalty programs, and rewards.

Your customers access your menu and place orders through your public ordering page. There are three account types: anonymous (no login required), lite (staff adds their email or phone so loyalty points accumulate and can be applied by staff at the customer's request), and full (customers log in to view and redeem their points themselves).

Auto Onboarding is a quick setup wizard that creates your restaurant and admin account in minutes. You will create your account, enter your restaurant details, and be ready to manage your restaurant from the dashboard.
How It Works

The onboarding flow is a single step. You enter your email, password, restaurant name, address, phone number, and a short description. Your URL is automatically generated from your restaurant name. Once you submit, your account is created and you are taken directly to the dashboard.
Tips for a Successful Setup

items: Take time to set up your menu with clear categories and descriptions — it makes ordering easier for customers
Upload high-quality photos for your menu items to increase order rates
Configure your service hours and fulfillment options in Settings so customers know when to expect their order
Test an order through the customer view to verify the full flow

blocks.body: The Order Board, or Tablero, is your live command center. All incoming orders appear here in real time, organized by status. You can view order details, update statuses, modify items, process payments, and print receipts — all from one screen.
Ticket Lifecycle

A ticket moves through four active states plus two endings. Staff press the advance button on a ticket to move it forward; a guest check-out or a staff-created order starts it at the first active state:

items: NEW (INCOMPLETE) — the ticket exists but the order has not been sent to the kitchen yet. Nothing is prepared from it.
COMPLETE — the order is placed and the kitchen ticket can be printed. Customers see it as confirmed.
ACCEPTED — the kitchen has taken the order and is preparing it.
READY — the order is finished and can be picked up or delivered. The customer is notified automatically.
PAID — payment has been taken. The ticket leaves the live board and moves into Reporting.
CANCELLED — the ticket was cancelled.

blocks.body: The advance button follows the same order in both apps: COMPLETE → ACCEPTED → READY → PAID. Pressing it while a ticket is at PAID opens the payment screen instead of advancing further.
Customer Status Updates

When a ticket advances, the customer is notified automatically. A customer who placed the order online sees the progress steps — confirmed, preparing, ready — and receives a push notification when the order is ready, even if they closed the ordering page.
Ticket Age Badge

Each ticket on the board carries an age badge. It counts from the moment the ticket was completed for a ticket that has completed, and from the moment it was created for one that has not. The badge changes color as the ticket gets older and starts flashing when it has been waiting a long time, so the oldest tickets are easy to spot.
How to find this: Side menu → Orders (web)  |  Bottom nav → Pedidos (mobile)

items: NEW (INCOMPLETE) — the ticket exists but the order has not been sent to the kitchen yet.
COMPLETE — the order is placed and the kitchen ticket can be printed. Customers see it as confirmed.
ACCEPTED — the kitchen has taken the order and is preparing it.
READY — the order is finished and can be picked up or delivered.
PAID — payment has been taken. The ticket leaves the live board.
CANCELLED — the ticket was cancelled.

blocks.body: Working with Orders

Click on any order card to open its details panel. Large orders are visually enlarged on the board so you can prioritize them at a glance. From the details panel you can make the following adjustments:

items: Update the order status
Add or remove items
Edit item quantities
Add or remove modifiers
Apply promotions and discounts
Transfer the order to another table
Add internal notes
Process payments with the on-screen keypad

blocks.body: The payment keypad supports the full checkout flow: enter the amount received (cash or card), calculate change automatically, open the cash drawer, and print a customer receipt.
All adjustments sync in real time across all connected devices.
Sound & Visual Alerts
When a new order arrives, a notification sound plays and the board flashes. You can mute the sound from the header bar if needed.

Push notifications extend this beyond the app. Enable admin push notifications to receive alerts for new orders even when your device is locked or the app is closed. Guest push notifications keep your customers informed — they receive updates when their order status changes even if they have closed the ordering page.
Offline Handling

Orders are cached locally on your device. If your internet connection drops, you can continue viewing, updating, and processing payments. All changes are synced automatically when the connection is restored. The sync indicator in the header shows your current connection status.
Loyalty Points on Orders
When you take an order as an admin, you play a key role in helping your customers earn loyalty points. Here is how it works:

items: If the customer orders without providing any details (anonymous), they will not earn points. However, if loyalty is activated, the receipt shows how many points they would have earned — encouraging them to create an account next time.

If the customer provides their email or phone number, a lite account is created automatically. Points accumulate on their behalf. On future visits, they can give their phone number again to access their points, and you can apply rewards at their request.

If the customer later logs in using the app with the same email or phone number, their lite account converts to a full password-protected account. All their points are preserved and they can redeem rewards themselves.

blocks.body: The Menu section lets you build and manage your entire menu — schedules, categories, items, modifiers, combos, and images. Changes you make are reflected immediately in your customer-facing ordering page.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Update menu (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Update Menu (mobile)
Menu Schedule

Each menu has its own schedule that controls when it is available for ordering. Your guests can install your restaurant's app directly from your website — it works like a native app without going through an app store. If the menu's schedule marks the restaurant as closed, guests cannot place orders. This prevents orders on holidays, vacations, or after hours, so setting the schedule correctly is essential.
Multiple Menus

You can create multiple menus with different schedules. For example, create a Breakfast menu available from 6am to 11am and a Lunch / Dinner menu for the rest of the day. Each menu holds its own categories, items, and schedule. If you only need one set of items available all day, a single menu is sufficient.
Categories

Categories organize your menu items into a hierarchy up to three levels deep. For example: Drinks → Hot Drinks → Coffees. You can create categories, sub-categories, and sub-sub-categories, and move items between them at any time.
Menu Items

Create menu items with a name, description, price, and optional photo. Assign each item to a category, sub-category, or sub-sub-category. Items can be moved to a different category after creation. You can also toggle items as available or unavailable without deleting them.
Combos

Combos let you bundle multiple menu items together at a special price. For example, a Combo Meal might include a main item, a side, and a drink for a discounted price. When a customer adds a combo to their order, all included items are added together.
Modifiers

Modifiers let customers customize their items with options that adjust the price. Common examples include size options (Small, Medium, Large), spice levels, and extra toppings. Each modifier has a name and an optional price that gets added to the bill.
Notes vs Modifiers

Notes are free-form text that customers or staff can add to any menu item — for allergies, special requests, or unique instructions. Notes do NOT add cost to the bill. If you want to charge for extras, always create a modifier instead.

Modifiers also speed up order processing. Staff can add common instructions like "no onion" or "well done" with a single tap instead of typing them out on a device keyboard. The more modifiers you create, the more uniform your orders become and the easier it is to track what your customers are ordering.
Images
You can upload photos for your menu items. High-quality images help customers decide what to order. Supported formats include JPEG, PNG, and WebP.

Promotions let you offer discounts and special deals to your customers. You can create percentage-based discounts, fixed amount discounts, or free item offers. Promotions can be scheduled for specific days or date ranges.
How to find this: Side menu → Marketing → Promotions (web)  |  Bottom nav → Marketing → Promotions (mobile)
Value to Customers
Promotions attract new customers and encourage repeat visits. A well-timed discount can boost sales during slow periods. Limited-time offers create urgency and drive more orders.
How to Set Up

Go to the Promotions section in your admin dashboard. Click Create Promotion. Choose a discount type (percentage off, fixed amount off, or free item), set the discount value, optionally link it to specific menu items, and set the active dates. You can enable or disable promotions at any time.
How It Works

When a customer opens the guest app, any active promotions are displayed immediately. The customer can select an applicable promotion when placing an order, and the discount is applied to their total before payment.
Technical Details

Promotions can be item-specific (applied to a particular menu item) or order-wide (applied to the entire order). Multiple promotions cannot be stacked on the same order. Promotions that require a menu item will be removed automatically if the item is removed from the order. Expired promotions are hidden from customers but preserved in your history.
The loyalty program lets you reward your regular customers with points that can be redeemed for discounts or free items. This encourages repeat business and builds customer loyalty.
How to find this: Side menu → Marketing → Loyalty programs (web)  |  Bottom nav → Marketing → Loyalty (mobile)
Value to Customers
Customers earn points on every order, which they can redeem for rewards. This gives them a reason to choose your restaurant over competitors and keeps them coming back.
How to Set Up

Go to the Loyalty section in your admin dashboard. First, set the points multiplier — this determines how many points customers earn per dollar spent. For example, a multiplier of 10 means a $10 order earns 100 points.
Next, create rewards. Each reward needs a name, description, and the number of points required to redeem it. You can choose the reward type:

items: Discount on order — a fixed amount or percentage off the total
Free item — select a specific menu item that the customer receives for free

blocks.body: Once your rewards are created, toggle the program on to activate it. You can enable or disable individual rewards at any time without losing accumulated points.
How It Works
When a customer places an order through a lite or full account, they earn points based on the order total and your points multiplier. Points are tracked per customer and per restaurant location.
How points are redeemed depends on the account type:

items: Anonymous — the customer can see available rewards but needs to create an account to redeem them
Lite — staff adds the customer's email or phone so points accumulate. Staff can apply rewards at the customer's request from the admin panel
Full — the customer logs in and can view their points and apply rewards themselves during checkout

blocks.body: Active rewards and loyalty information are also visible in the guest app, so customers always know what rewards are available and how many points they have.
How Guest Points Work in Practice
Loyalty must first be activated in Settings → Features before it can be used. Once active, here is how points work depending on how the customer interacts with your restaurant:

items: Guest orders through the app without logging in — they see loyalty info but earn no points. The receipt shows how many points they would have gained, encouraging them to create an account.
Guest orders through the app and logs in — they earn points and can redeem rewards immediately. Full loyalty benefits apply.
Admin takes an anonymous order — the customer gets no points, but the receipt displays potential points if loyalty is active.

Admin takes an order and the customer provides their email or phone — a lite account is created. Points accumulate and are available on every future visit. Staff can apply rewards at the customer's request.

Admin takes an order, the customer provides their email or phone, and later logs in using the app — the lite account converts to a full password-protected account. All their points are preserved and they can now view and redeem rewards directly.

blocks.body: Fulfillment types determine how customers receive their orders. You can choose from three options: Eat-in, Pickup / Curbside, and Delivery.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Restaurant setup (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Restaurant Setup (mobile)
Delivery
Customers enter their delivery address and place their order. The order appears on your board with the delivery address. You prepare the order and arrange delivery.
Pickup
Customers place an order and come to your restaurant to pick it up. The estimated preparation time is displayed during checkout.
Curbside
Customers place an order, drive to your location, and you bring the order to their car.
Eat-In / Dine-In

Customers place an order from their table using a QR code. The order is sent to the kitchen, and staff can deliver it to the table when ready. This requires setting up tables with QR codes linked to your menu.
Configuring Fulfillment
Go to Settings and enable the fulfillment types you want to offer. For dine-in, create tables in the Tables section and print QR code tent cards.

DirectEatz supports electronic invoicing (DTE) for El Salvador. When enabled, paid tickets are emitted to Hacienda (the Ministerio de Hacienda) as electronic documents. This section explains every field on the DTE setup page so you can configure it correctly the first time.
DTE Toggle

The toggle at the top of the page enables or disables electronic invoicing. When OFF, paid tickets are normal receipts. When ON, every paid ticket is automatically emitted to Hacienda as a DTE. The toggle is disabled until you have saved a valid emisor configuration and uploaded your certificate.
Step 1 — Upload Your Hacienda Certificate

Before filling in the emisor fields, upload your certificate first. Go to the Certificate card, click "Choose file", and select the XML file you downloaded from the Hacienda portal (portal.dte.gob.sv). Then click "Upload Certificate". The system will parse the XML and automatically fill in your NIT, NRC, and Business Name. You still need to fill in all other fields manually.
Do not share your Hacienda certificate XML file with anyone. Anyone who has this file can issue invoices under your business name.
Step 2 — Emisor Configuration
The emisor is the business issuing the invoice. Fill in every field exactly as registered with Hacienda. All values here are printed on every electronic invoice your customers receive.
Ambiente

Select which Hacienda environment to use. Use "Pruebas (00)" while setting up and testing — invoices sent in this mode are test documents and do not count as real tax invoices. Switch to "Producción (01)" only when you are ready to issue legally binding invoices. You can switch back to Pruebas at any time for testing.
NIT

Your Número de Identificación Tributaria — a 14-digit number assigned by Hacienda. This is your business's tax ID. Example: 94500201851069. If you uploaded your certificate, this field is filled automatically. Do not modify it unless you know it is incorrect.
NRC
Your Registro Nacional de Contribuyentes number. This is your business's taxpayer registration number with Hacienda. Example: 3899028. Auto-filled from the certificate if uploaded.
Business Name (Razón Social)

The full legal name of your company exactly as it appears on your Hacienda registration. This is the name that appears as the issuer on every invoice. Example: "Restaurante El Buen Sabor, S.A. de C.V." Auto-filled from the certificate if uploaded.
Commercial Name (Nombre Comercial)
The trade name your customers know you by. This can be the same as your Business Name or a shorter name. Example: "El Buen Sabor". This name also appears on the invoice.
Activity Code (Código de Actividad)

The economic activity code from your Hacienda registration. This is a 4 or 5-digit code that describes what your business does. Common codes for restaurants: 56110 (Restaurant services), 56120 (Cafeterías), 56200 (Catering). You can look up your code on the Hacienda portal or in your registration documents.
Activity Description (Descripción de Actividad)

A short text description of the activity code above. Example: "Prestación de servicios de restaurante" or "Servicios de preparación de alimentos". This must match the official description for your activity code in the Hacienda catalog.
Establishment Type (Tipo de Establecimiento)

A 2-digit code describing the type of establishment. The most common values are: "01" for General (a standard business location), "02" for Casa Matriz (headquarters/main office), and "09" for Depósito Fiscal (bonded warehouse). Use "01" unless Hacienda has assigned you a different code.
Establishment Code (Código de Establecimiento MH)

A code assigned by Hacienda to identify your specific establishment (physical location). This is not the same as the Establishment Type. If Hacienda has not assigned you a specific code, leave this field blank. You can find this code on your Hacienda portal under your registered establishments.
Point of Sale Code (Código de Punto de Venta)

A code that identifies your point of sale (caja/register) within the establishment. This is your internal code — you define it yourself. For example, if you have one register, use "001". If you have multiple, use "001", "002", etc. This helps Hacienda track which register issued each invoice.
Point of Sale Code MH (Código de Punto de Venta MH)

The point of sale code as assigned by Hacienda (not your internal code). If Hacienda has not assigned you a specific point of sale code, leave this field blank. You can find this on the Hacienda portal under your registered points of sale.
Address (Dirección)

The street address or complement of your establishment. This is the detailed address line — for example: "Calle Principal #123, Colonia San Benito". This appears on the invoice as the issuer's address.
Phone (Teléfono)
Your business phone number. Use the format with country code if needed, for example: 2222-1234 or +503 2222-1234. This appears on the invoice.
Email (Correo)
Your business email address. Hacienda uses this to send you notifications about your DTE submissions. It also appears on invoices so customers can contact you.
Department (Departamento)

A 2-digit code for the department (state) where your establishment is located. Example: 01 for San Salvador, 02 for Santa Ana, 06 for La Libertad, 10 for Usulután. You can find the full list in the Hacienda catalog at catalogos.dte.gob.sv.
Municipality (Municipio)

A 2-digit code for the municipality within the department. Example: for department 02 (Santa Ana), use 17 for Santa Ana Oeste, 01 for Santa Ana Centro. The valid municipality codes depend on the department you selected. Find yours in the Hacienda catalog at catalogos.dte.gob.sv.
District (Distrito)

A 2-digit code for the district within the municipality. This is only required in some departments. If your department does not use districts, leave this field blank. Check the Hacienda catalog to see if your municipality requires a district code.

Department, Municipality, and District codes are all 2 digits and can be found in the Hacienda catalog at catalogos.dte.gob.sv. Each department has its own set of municipalities, and each municipality may have its own set of districts.
Step 3 — Hacienda API Credentials
These credentials are your login for the Hacienda DTE portal (portal.dte.gob.sv). DirectEatz uses them to authenticate when sending invoices to Hacienda on your behalf.
API Username (Usuario API)
Your Hacienda portal username. This is the same username you use to log in to portal.dte.gob.sv to download your certificate and manage your DTE settings.
API Password (Clave API)
Your Hacienda portal password. This is stored securely and used only to authenticate API requests to Hacienda.
Step 4 — SMTP / Email Delivery (Optional)

If you want DirectEatz to automatically email DTE invoices to your customers, configure your SMTP settings here. This is optional — invoices are always saved in the DTE History regardless of SMTP settings.
SMTP Host

The hostname of your email server. Examples: smtp.gmail.com (Gmail), smtp.office365.com (Microsoft 365), smtp-relay.gmail.com (Google Workspace). If you use a hosting provider, check their documentation for the SMTP host.
SMTP Port
The port number for your email server. Common values: 587 for TLS (recommended), 465 for SSL, 25 for unencrypted (not recommended). Default is 587.
SMTP Username
The username or email address for your SMTP account. For Gmail, this is your full email address (e.g., restaurant@gmail.com).
SMTP Password

The password for your SMTP account. If you use Gmail or Microsoft 365, you may need to create an App Password instead of using your regular login password. Check your email provider's documentation for details.
Step 5 — Test and Enable
1. After saving your emisor configuration, click "Test Emit" to send a test DTE to Hacienda. This verifies that your certificate, emisor details, and API credentials all work together.
2. If the test succeeds, you will see a confirmation message. If it fails, check each field for typos — especially NIT, NRC, department/municipality codes, and your Hacienda portal login.
3. Once the test passes, toggle DTE to enabled at the top of the page. From this point on, every paid ticket will be automatically emitted to Hacienda as an electronic invoice.
Keep Ambiente on "Pruebas (00)" until your test emission succeeds. Only switch to "Producción (01)" when you are ready to issue real, legally binding invoices.
What Gets Auto-Filled

When you upload your Hacienda certificate, the system extracts and fills in your NIT, NRC, and Business Name automatically. All other fields — Activity Code, Activity Description, Establishment Type, Establishment Code, Point of Sale Codes, Address, Phone, Email, Department, Municipality, and District — must be filled in manually.
DTE Document Statuses

items: Pending — The DTE has been created and queued but not yet sent to Hacienda. This usually means your connection is down or Hacienda's API is temporarily unavailable.
Sent — The DTE was successfully received and accepted by Hacienda. The invoice is now a valid tax document.
Failed — The DTE could not be sent. Common causes: expired certificate, wrong API credentials, invalid data in the emisor fields, or Hacienda's system is down. Fix the issue and retry.
Anulled — The DTE was annulled (cancelled) after being sent. Annulled invoices cannot be reversed — you must issue a new invoice if needed.

blocks.body: Viewing Sent Documents (DTE History)

The DTE History section shows all DTE documents that have been emitted, along with their status, type, date, and DTE number. You can filter by status and date range, export to CSV, and view or print individual invoices.
Contingency Mode
Choosing Your Address Codes

The Department, Municipality and District fields pick from the official Hacienda catalogs. Department offers the full list of El Salvador's departments; Municipality narrows to the municipalities of the department you chose; District narrows again to the districts of that municipality. Each field can be left blank if your address does not use it.
The codes offered are the official ones, so the lists already match the Hacienda catalog — pick from them rather than typing a code by hand.

If your internet connection is down when you try to emit a DTE, the document is stored locally and queued. When connectivity is restored, the pending documents are sent automatically. If a DTE remains pending for an extended period, you can use the Flush Contingency button to force-send all queued documents.
The Tables section lets you manage your physical tables and generate QR codes so customers can order from their table. Each table gets a unique QR code that links directly to your menu.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Tables (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Tables (mobile)
Value to Customers

QR codes do more than let customers order from their table. Each person at the table can create their own separate order — no more confusion over split tickets or waiting 20 minutes for a server to take a large group's orders. Once an order is completed, guests can place another one without waiting. Customers can also install the guest app directly from the ordering page and order from home in the future, increasing your overall revenue.
How to Set Up

Go to the Tables section. Add your tables by name or number (e.g., Table 1, Patio 3). You can also create sections for different areas (Indoor, Patio, Bar). Once tables are created, you can download or print QR codes for each table. Place the QR tent cards on the tables so customers can scan and order.
How It Works

When a customer scans the QR code, they are taken to your ordering page with the table pre-selected. They add items to their order and submit. You receive the order on your board with the table number displayed, so you know where to deliver it.
Payments are processed directly from the order screen using the on-screen keypad. Two payment types are available: Cash and Card.
How to Process a Payment

Open the order details and tap the payment keypad. Select Cash or Card, then enter the amount received. For cash payments, change is calculated automatically. For card payments, enter the confirmation code provided by your card terminal.
Reporting
The Reports section shows a breakdown of payments by type (cash vs card) along with card confirmation codes, so you can reconcile your transactions.
The Personnel section lets you manage your staff accounts and control what each team member can do in the admin dashboard. You can add, remove, and set granular permissions.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Personnel (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Personnel (mobile)
Permissions
Each staff member can be given one or more permissions. Instead of predefined roles, you simply toggle the permissions each person needs:

items: OWNER — Full access to all settings, billing, and management. Only the restaurant owner has this permission.
UPDATE MENU — Add, edit, and remove menu items, categories, modifiers, and combos, and change the menu schedule.
UPDATE LOYALTY — Create and manage promotions and loyalty programs.
UPDATE RESTAURANT — Change restaurant information, features, color theme, and tables.
UPDATE PERSONNEL — Add, remove, and manage staff accounts and their permissions.
ADJUST ORDERS — Controls whether the staff member can open and modify closed tickets in the reporting section. Disabling this prevents untrustworthy admins from altering past orders.

SEE TOTALS — Controls whether the staff member can see the total sales amount for the selected time period in reports. Disabling this hides revenue data from staff you don't want seeing how much the business made.

blocks.body: Adding Staff
There are two steps to add a staff member:

items: The staff member creates their own account using the app or website at directEatz.com. They enter their email, name, and choose a password.
In the Personnel section, click Add new user and enter the staff member's email to link them to your restaurant. They will appear in the list and you can set their permissions.

blocks.body: Removing Staff

In the Personnel section, click on a staff member and tap Remove. This unlinks them from your restaurant — their account is not deleted, so they can be re-linked later if needed. The owner cannot be removed.
The Printers section lets you connect network printers so tickets print directly in the kitchen or wherever you need them.
Two Printer Slots

Every restaurant has two printer slots, and every printer you add can be assigned to either one. Both slots are per-device settings — each tablet or computer chooses which printer it uses for each slot, so the front counter and the kitchen can print to different devices.

items: Kitchen printer — the printer that receives kitchen tickets automatically. This is the printer the silent-print switch uses. Tap the switch next to a printer to make it this device's kitchen printer.
Guest printer — the printer that receives the customer receipt at check-out. Tap the switch next to a printer to make it this device's guest printer.

blocks.body: Silent Print (Restaurant-wide Switch)

Silent print is a restaurant-level switch in Settings → Printers. When it is on, every device that can physically reach a kitchen printer prints kitchen tickets by itself as soon as an order is placed — no buttons, no print dialogs. When it is off, nothing prints automatically and staff print manually. Manual print buttons always work regardless of the switch.
How the Devices Decide Who Prints

When silent print is on, the devices coordinate so exactly one kitchen ticket prints per order. The device that created the order tries first; if it has no kitchen printer, it asks for help and the ticket is handed to the first device that can print it. If a printer refuses the job, that device steps out and another takes over — a wrong IP address or a powered-off printer never blocks the kitchen.
Print Status on Every Ticket

While an order is waiting to print, the ticket shows a small spinning indicator. It keeps spinning until the kitchen printer confirms the ticket, then it clears. If nothing confirms after five minutes, the indicator turns into a warning state so you can see which orders never reached the printer.
Print Problems

When a ticket cannot be printed, the order card shows a "Print did not work" notice after a minute. Printing the ticket manually from the order clears it — the manual print confirms the ticket for every device. The notice can also mean the printer is off, the IP address is wrong, or the paper is out, so check the printer itself first.

Silent print needs a network printer (ESC/POS over your Wi-Fi) or the DirectEatz relay service. A plain browser printing through the computer's print dialog can never be the automatic kitchen printer.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Printers (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Printers (mobile)
Setting Up a Printer

Printers connect over your WiFi network. To set one up, you need the printer’s IP address. For most thermal printers, you can find the IP by printing a self-test page (hold the feed button while powering on) or checking the printer’s Settings menu under Network or Wi-Fi.

Once you have the IP, go to the Printers section and click Add Printer. Give it a name (e.g. “Kitchen”), enter the IP address, and select the paper width in millimeters (usually 58mm or 80mm for thermal printers). Print a test receipt and adjust the width mm as needed.
Connection Types

items: Network printer (TCP) — Connects directly to a thermal printer over your network using ESC/POS commands. The ticket prints immediately without any print dialog or preview. This is the best option for restaurants because it works silently in the background — kitchen tickets print the moment an order comes in, with no staff interaction needed. Requires a printer that supports TCP connections on your local network.

Traditional (Normal print) — Opens your browser’s print dialog. Works with any printer connected to the device (thermal, inkjet, laser, etc.). Disadvantage: Staff must interact with the print preview dialog before the ticket prints.

Relay — Browsers cannot send raw network requests, so the relay option lets you install a small relay server on your network that receives print jobs from the browser and forwards them to the printer over TCP. This adds some complexity but enables printing from any device running the admin dashboard.

blocks.body: Auto Print (Silent Printing)

When Auto Print is turned on, a kitchen ticket prints automatically as soon as a new order comes in — no buttons to press. Kitchen staff are alerted immediately and can start preparing. When off, staff must manually print tickets.
Ticket Printing Options

There are two types of tickets: a kitchen ticket (for the kitchen staff to prepare the order) and a customer ticket (a receipt for the guest). The native app lets you choose which type to print. Auto Print always sends a kitchen ticket, and the checkout flow always sends a customer ticket. Kitchen tickets always group items and include notes — the toggles below only affect customer receipts.

items: Simple print (customer ticket) — Groups identical items with a combined quantity (e.g. “3 × Burger $27.00”) instead of listing each item on its own line. Makes tickets shorter and easier to read.
Print notes (customer ticket) — Prints any special instructions or notes the customer added to their items (e.g. “no onions”, “extra sauce”) on the ticket.

blocks.body: Using Printers Across Devices
Once a printer is added, every device connected to your restaurant can see and select it. Just go to Settings → Printers and toggle on the printer you want to use on that device.
Editing a Printer
Click on an existing printer in the list to update its name, IP address, paper width, or connection type. Changes take effect immediately.
The Reports section shows your sales and order history. Filter by date range to review past activity.

The Reports section is also where you review past tickets. The permission that controls whether past orders can be reopened and changed here is ADJUST ORDERS — staff without it get a read-only view. The same permission is what makes the Reporting menu item appear for a staff member.
The SEE TOTALS permission controls whether the revenue amounts appear in these reports. Staff without it still see the order list and ticket details, but the money columns are hidden.
How to find this: Side menu → Reporting (web)  |  Bottom nav → Informes (mobile)
Sales by Date
Use the date filter at the top to select a time period. The report shows a list of all orders within that range with basic details: ticket number, total, items, timestamp, and payments.
Viewing Past Orders
Click on any order to see full ticket details. If the staff member has the ADJUST ORDERS permission, they can reopen and make changes to closed tickets. Without it, past orders are view-only.
The Settings section is where you configure your restaurant’s features, information, appearance, and staff access.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings (mobile)
Restaurant Setup
Features
Toggle which fulfillment types and features are available for your customers:

items: Delivery — Enables online ordering for delivery. Customers enter their address and pay online. Requires a Delivery feature for the guest checkout flow.
Eat-in — Enables dine-in ordering. Customers can order from their table using the guest app. Shows table number on kitchen tickets.
Curbside — Enables curbside pickup. Customers check in when they arrive and staff are notified.
Loyalty — Enables the loyalty points program. Customers earn points on orders and can redeem rewards.

blocks.body: Restaurant Information

Set your restaurant name, phone number, address, city, and default tip percentage. The tip percentage only applies to Eat-in orders — it is added to the grand total automatically as a service charge. This information appears on your customer-facing ordering page and printed receipts.
About Us
Write a short description of your restaurant that appears on the guest ordering page.
Images
Upload photos of your restaurant. Images are displayed on the customer-facing ordering page.
Customer App Colors
Choose a color theme for your guest-facing pages.
The Billing section shows your current plan, balance, and a chronological history of plan changes, invoices, and payments.
How to find this: Side menu → Dashboard (web)  |  Bottom nav → Dashboard (mobile)
How Billing Works

DirectEatz uses monthly subscription plans. You are billed on the 1st of each month for the previous month's usage. The first month is pro-rated from your activation date. There are three plans available:

items: Starter ($14.99/mo) — For small restaurants
Restaurant ($39.99/mo) — For growing restaurants
Enterprise ($99.99/mo) — For restaurant chains

blocks.body: Upgrading Your Plan

You can upgrade to a higher plan at any time. When you upgrade mid-month, you are charged a pro-rated amount for the remaining days: the days at your current plan price plus the days at the new plan price. Select a plan card above your current plan to see a preview of the upgrade cost.
Billing Summary

The summary card at the top shows your current plan (with monthly price) and your current balance. The balance is calculated from the most recent invoice and reflects any unpaid amounts carried forward.
Billing History

The timeline shows all billing events in chronological order: plan activations (blue), monthly invoices (orange), payments received (green), and other charges (red). Each invoice shows the service month, the plan that was active, and the cumulative amount owed.
The TV Menu Display section gives you a link you can open on any TV or monitor in your restaurant to show your menu to customers.
How to find this: Side menu → Dashboard → TV Display (web)  |  Bottom nav → TV Display (mobile)
Setting Up
Go to the TV Display section and open the link on a TV or monitor connected to the internet. The page displays your menu in a full-screen format that updates automatically when you make changes.
The QR Codes section provides QR codes for your guest ordering page, admin dashboard, and mobile app download links. Print and display them so customers can easily access your online ordering.
How to find this: Side menu → Dashboard → QR Codes (web)  |  Bottom nav → QR Code (mobile)
Available QR Codes

items: Guest App — Links to your restaurant’s ordering page. Customers scan to browse your menu and place orders.
Admin — Links to your admin dashboard. Useful for quick access on a second device.
Google Play — Links to the DirectEatz app on the Google Play Store for Android devices.
App Store — Links to the DirectEatz app on the Apple App Store for iOS devices.

blocks.body: Each QR code can be downloaded as a PNG image for printing on tables, menus, or signage.

DirectEatz is designed to work even when your internet connection is unreliable. Orders, menu changes, and settings are stored locally on your device and synchronized with the server when connectivity is available.
Three Ways Devices Stay in Sync
Your devices keep each other up to date through three independent routes, and any one of them is enough on its own:

items: Server sync — the normal route. Every device exchanges tickets with the DirectEatz server, which is the only place guest orders, payments and loyalty are settled.
Wi-Fi device-to-device (P2P) — when devices are on the same Wi-Fi network they find each other and exchange tickets directly, with no internet and no server at all.
Cross-network relay (RTC pod) — devices on different networks, such as the store on Wi-Fi and an owner's tablet on cellular, keep syncing through a relay service when the server cannot be reached.

blocks.body: All three carry the same tickets in the same format, so it does not matter which route a particular ticket took — every device ends up with the same state.
What Syncs and What Does Not

Tickets, menu changes, settings, printer setup and staff changes all sync. Guest-facing things — taking an online order, settling a payment, loyalty points — always go through the server, because that is where the customer's order actually comes from.
How Quickly Changes Appear

On a good connection, a change made on one device appears on another within a few seconds. On a slow connection it can take longer, and when a device is offline its changes appear once it reconnects. The header indicator shows the current state.
How Sync Works

Every action you take (creating an order, updating the menu, applying a promotion) is recorded as a log entry. These logs are stored locally and sent to the server in batches. The server replays the logs in order to reconstruct the current state. This guarantees that no data is lost and all devices see the same state after sync.
Offline Operation

If your internet connection drops, you can continue working normally. Orders can be created, modified, and completed offline. When the connection is restored, all changes are synced automatically. The sync indicator in the header shows your current status: connected, syncing, or offline.
Best Practices

Keep your device connected to the internet when possible to ensure timely sync. If you notice the sync indicator showing offline for an extended period, check your network connection. Changes made on one device may take a few seconds to appear on another device after syncing.
Your data is encrypted in transit and protected by secure authentication.
Authentication
All admin users log in with a username and password. Sessions are managed with secure tokens that refresh automatically. Passwords are stored securely and never exposed.
Data Privacy

Customer data is stored securely and used only for order processing and loyalty programs. Each restaurant location only has access to its own data. Guest information is never shared between different restaurants.
Choose a color scheme that best matches your restaurant. This color will be shown to your guests when they open your restaurant's guest app by scanning the QR code on the table.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Customer App Colors (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Colors (mobile)

devices.web: Side menu → Settings → Customer App Colors

blocks.body: How It Works
When you download the table QR code image, it will use this color as well so your guests' entire experience is color-coded. The preview below shows how your selection will appear to customers.
Activate or deactivate features for your restaurant. Toggle each feature on or off to enable or disable it for your location.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Functions (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Functions (mobile)
What Each Feature Controls

Features control which capabilities are available to your staff and guests. For example, enabling online ordering allows guests to place orders through the guest app, while loyalty programs let customers earn rewards.
View detailed sales reports and order history. Analyze your restaurant's performance with filtering by date ranges and time periods.
How to find this: Side menu → Reporting (web)  |  Bottom nav → Informes (mobile)
Filtering Reports

Use the date pickers and time range chips to filter your report. You can view today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, or last month. The report updates automatically when you change the date range.
Exporting Data
Click the download button to export your report as a CSV file. This file can be opened in Excel or other spreadsheet applications for further analysis.
A comprehensive view of your restaurant's performance. Analyze revenue, orders, guests, and more with interactive charts and detailed tables.
How to find this: Side menu → Analytics (web)  |  Bottom nav → Analytics (mobile)
Date Filtering

Use the date pickers and quick range chips to filter your analytics. You can view today, yesterday, this week, last week, this month, or last month. The dashboard updates automatically when you change the date range. You can select up to 93 days of data.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
The KPI cards at the top show your most important metrics at a glance:

items: Total Revenue — the total sales amount for the selected period.
Orders — the total number of orders placed.
Average Order Value — the average amount spent per order.
Items Sold — the total number of menu items sold.
Unique Guests — the number of different customers who placed orders.

blocks.body: Revenue Trend
A bar chart showing your daily revenue over the selected time period. This helps you identify trends and patterns in your sales performance.
Top Items

Shows your best-selling menu items ranked by quantity sold. The horizontal bar chart visualizes which items are most popular, while the table below provides detailed revenue and quantity data for each item.
Fulfillment Breakdown
A pie chart and table showing how orders are being fulfilled (e.g., dine-in, takeout, delivery). This helps you understand which order types are most common at your restaurant.
Orders Over Time
A bar chart showing the number of orders placed each day. This is useful for identifying busy days and planning staffing accordingly.
Guest Analytics
A table showing your customers' ordering behavior including their name, email, number of orders, total amount spent, and loyalty points earned. This helps you identify your most valuable customers.
Promotions Performance

A table showing how your promotions are performing. It includes the promotion name, type, number of redemptions, and points redeemed. This helps you evaluate which promotions drive the most engagement.
Exporting Data
Click the download button at the bottom to save a screenshot of your analytics dashboard as an image file. This is useful for sharing reports or keeping records.
Manage your restaurant's menu. Create and edit menus, categories, subcategories, items, and combos.
How to find this: Side menu → Settings → Update menu (web)  |  Bottom nav → Settings → Update Menu (mobile)
Menu Management
Select a menu from the top buttons to view and edit it. You can create multiple menus for different purposes (e.g., dine-in, takeout, catering).
Adding Content

items: Categories — group related items together (e.g. Appetizers, Mains, Desserts).
Subcategories — organize items further inside a category.
Items — individual menu items with name, price, description and image.
Combos — bundle several items together at a special price.

blocks.body: Editing Items
Tap on any item to edit its details. You can update the name, price, description, and image. Changes are saved automatically and appear on your guest app in real-time.

On Windows laptops the network adapter can enter a low-power state after a few minutes without user activity. When that happens, peer-to-peer discovery and sync between your devices stops until you move the mouse or press a key. Apply these power settings once on every Windows machine that runs DirectEatz.
Power Settings

items: Device Manager → Wi-Fi adapter → Power Management → uncheck "Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power"
Power Options → Advanced → Wireless Adapter Settings → Power Saving Mode → Maximum Performance (both on battery and plugged in)
Adapter Advanced tab → disable the driver-specific power save (Intel "Power Saving Mode", Realtek "Advanced Power Save") and EEE
PCI Express → Link State Power Management → Off
Sleep → Never (when plugged in)

blocks.body: The Floor Map shows your dining room the way it really is — tables, walls, the bar and decorations placed to match the physical space — and doubles as a live view of which tables have open orders.
View Mode

The map shows every table you have created, at its real position and size. A table with open orders is highlighted, and each table shows how many open tickets it has. Tap a table to open its ticket sheet: you can see the open tickets for that table, start a new order for it, or print its QR card.
Edit Mode
Switch to edit mode to place your furniture. The room is a fixed 8 × 8 metre square, so everything you place has to fit inside it.

items: Tables — seven square table sizes, from two seats up to eight. Drag to move, use the size control to scale, and rotate to match the room.
Bar — a long counter piece.
Walls — four lengths (1, 2, 3 and 4 metres) for marking the edges of the room.
Plants — small and large, purely decorative.

blocks.body: Adding a table places it on the nearest free spot automatically; from there you drag it into place. Tables can be resized and rotated without ever leaving the room, and a new table can be bound to an existing table name or left unassigned.
Starting an Order from a Table

Tapping a table and starting a new order does two things at once: it attaches the table to the ticket and marks it as an eat-in order. The kitchen ticket then carries the table number, so staff know where to take it.
Printing Table QR Cards
Each table has its own QR code. Print the card from the table's ticket sheet and place it on the table so guests can scan, see the menu and order from their seats.
App settings are personal to the device you are holding — they do not change how the restaurant looks to customers, and they are not shared with other staff.
How to Find This

items: Web: the gear icon in the tablero header opens App Settings.
Mobile: side menu → App settings.

blocks.body: Notifications
Turn sound alerts for new orders on or off. This is the same mute control that appears in the tablero header, and it is per device — muting the front counter does not mute the kitchen.
Keep Screen On

Keeps the screen awake while the app is in the foreground, so a busy board does not lock itself in the middle of service. On a Windows computer this works together with the Windows power settings described in the Windows Setup section.
Dark Mode
Switches the admin app between light and dark appearance. This changes only your device.
Font Size
Adjusts the text size across the app. This changes only your device.
Switch Venue

Only staff who belong to more than one restaurant see this. It changes which restaurant this device is operating for. The switch happens online only, and every locally stored ticket for the current restaurant is pushed to the server before the device switches and reloads the new restaurant.
Connected Devices

Shows the other devices on your Wi-Fi network that are running DirectEatz for the same restaurant. Devices find each other automatically and exchange tickets directly, so service keeps running even if the internet goes down. If no devices appear, check that all devices are on the same Wi-Fi network.
RTC Pod

Shows whether this device is connected to the relay service that lets devices on different networks — for example the store on Wi-Fi and an owner's tablet at home on cellular — keep their tickets in sync when the server cannot be reached. The connection status is shown here and in the header.
Account
Change your password, log out, or delete your account. Logging out does not delete anything: tickets that have not synced yet stay on the device and are uploaded the next time you log in.
The Start screen is the restaurant's live overview — what is happening right now, how today is going, and the fastest way into the most common tasks.
Today at a Glance
The row of cards at the top shows the numbers that matter during service:

items: Occupied tables — how many of your tables currently have an open order, with a bar showing how full the room is.
Active orders — orders that have been placed but not paid yet.
Average preparation time — how long orders take from the kitchen accepting them to marking them ready, averaged over today's orders.
Today's revenue — the total taken so far today.
Delayed orders — orders that were placed more than 20 minutes ago and have still not been accepted by the kitchen. These are highlighted in red so they get attention first.

blocks.body: Today's Sales
A bar chart of today's paid orders by hour, so you can see the rush pattern and when the room was busiest.
Insight

A short, plain-language read on the current state of the room — whether the kitchen is falling behind, whether preparation times are running long, or whether it is a good moment to review the menu or promotions. Each insight has a shortcut straight to the relevant screen.
Quick Actions

Shortcuts to the most common screens: orders, new order, reporting, billing and settings. The list adapts to what your permissions allow — staff who cannot see billing do not see the billing shortcut.
Recent Activity
The latest ticket events across the restaurant: an order being confirmed, accepted by the kitchen, marked ready, paid, or a ticket printing successfully. Each entry shows who did it and how long ago.
DirectEatz presents the restaurant's Terms & Conditions once, before the admin app is used. One owner accepting them covers the whole restaurant.
How It Works

The first time the app is opened — and again whenever the terms are updated — the acceptance screen appears and the app cannot be used until somebody accepts. Any owner-level account can accept; the acceptance is recorded against the restaurant, not the person.
Once one owner has accepted, nobody else is asked again for that version. When the terms change, the new version has to be accepted once more.
What It Covers

The full wording is shown on the acceptance screen itself, in the language the device is set to. Accepting records the version and the time, and every device in the restaurant sees the same acceptance status.
A staff member can be linked to more than one restaurant. When that happens, the device can switch between them from App Settings.
Switching Restaurants
Open App Settings and use Switch Venue. The list shows every restaurant this account belongs to; tap the one you want. The switch happens online only, and only after the device confirms the switch.
What Happens to Your Tickets

Switching does not mix restaurants. Every locally stored ticket for the restaurant you are leaving is pushed to the server first; only when that upload succeeds does the device wipe its local data and reload the restaurant you chose. If the upload fails, nothing is wiped and you stay where you are.
This is why switching needs an internet connection: it would otherwise be possible to lose tickets that were taken offline and never uploaded.
